A_target.statement:
Let $M$ be a [[Definition:Smooth Manifold|smooth manifold]] and $p \in M$.
Then the [[Definition:Tangent Space|tangent space]] at $p$ is:
:$T_p M = \set {\gamma: \openint {-\epsilon} \epsilon \to M \text { smooth}, \map \gamma 0 = p} / \sim$
where $\gamma_1 \sim \gamma_2$ {{iff}} they agree to first order at $0$.

B_source.statement:
Let $f: A \to B$ be a [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]].
Then:
:$A / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$
where $\map \ker f$ identifies elements with the same image.

substitutions.the map whose kernel is collapsed: the map sending a curve to its derivative in a chart
substitutions.the kernel: curves whose chart derivative vanishes at p

derived.the image of the map: the vector space R^n in the chosen chart

object_map.reformulation: Curves do not form a group, so the kernel-quotient pattern must be reformulated at the level of equivalence relations induced by a map rather than of normal subgroups.

validity_conditions: the equivalence must be independent of the chart, which follows from the chain rule and invertibility of transition maps
the curves must be differentiable at the point for the derivative to be defined
the resulting quotient is a set-level quotient that inherits a vector space structure only via the chart identification
proof_plan:
Fix a [[Definition:Chart|chart]] $\phi$ around $p$ and map each curve $\gamma$ through $p$ to:
:$\map {\paren {\phi \circ \gamma}'} 0 \in \R^n$

For another chart $\psi$, by the [[Chain Rule for Real-Valued Functions|chain rule]]:
:$\map {\paren {\psi \circ \gamma}'} 0 = \map D {\psi \circ \phi^{-1} } \map {\paren {\phi \circ \gamma}'} 0$
As the transition [[Definition:Jacobian Matrix|Jacobian]] is invertible, $\sim$ does not depend on the chart.
By the isomorphism-theorem pattern, the quotient by $\sim$ is in bijection with the image, which is all of $\R^n$ since $t \mapsto \map {\phi^{-1} } {\map \phi p + t v}$ has derivative $v$.
